source: POLARIS v1.0 soil properties (Chaney et al., 2019), Duke University; grid from the NOAA NCEI nClimGrid reduced sample published in monocongo/example_climate_indices
subset_description: Total plant-available water capacity over a 0-1000 mm soil column, in millimetres, on a 3 x 3 subset of the nClimGrid grid used by the pinned low-res monthly example inputs (monocongo/example_climate_indices commit ae57c488af832c1ebfdf864c8ed7d16636e2e36f, 38 x 87 cells). The subset is latitude indices 20:23 (37.895832, 38.5625, 39.229168 degrees north) by longitude indices 36:39 (-100.6875, -100.020836, -99.354164 degrees east), the Colorado/Kansas border country. Values are derived by scripts/prepare_nclimgrid_awc_fixture.py from POLARIS v1.0 p50 van Genuchten parameters (alpha as log10(kPa^-1), n, theta_r, theta_s) over the five layers 0-5, 5-15, 15-30, 30-60 and 60-100 cm, area-weighted onto the subset's cell centres by climate_indices.aws_ingest. 180 publisher tiles were read; none are committed.
citation: Chaney, N. W., Minasny, B., Herman, J. D., Nauman, T. W., Brungard, C. W., Morgan, C. L. S., McBratney, A. B., Wood, E. F., and Yimam, Y. (2019): POLARIS soil properties: 30 m probabilistic maps of soil properties over the contiguous United States, Water Resources Research, 55(4), 2916-2938. Grid: Vose, R. S., Applequist, S., Squires, M., Durre, I., Menne, M. J., Williams, C. N. Jr., Fenimore, C., Gleason, K., and Arndt, D. (2014): NOAA Monthly U.S. Climate Gridded Dataset (NClimGrid), Version 1 [subset used], NOAA NCEI, DOI:10.7289/V5SX6B56.
license: POLARIS v1.0 is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (Attribution-NonCommercial), so this reduced, modified derivative must not be used commercially and must not be presented as an unaltered POLARIS product. The grid coordinates come from an NCEI nClimGrid derivative whose terms require attribution and prohibit implying NOAA endorsement.
notes: Development fixture, not a validation oracle: no external drought-index product was measured against it, so validation_tolerance.atol_mm is 0.0 and the tests assert the committed bytes rather than an external value. Do not describe it as an authoritative AWC dataset. Known limitations: (1) the derivation is available water for median MARGINAL parameters (p50), not the median of available water; (2) the p50 statistic and the 1000 mm column depth are a development choice, chosen because 1000 mm matches the USGS gNATSGO product's native 100-cm column and is reachable from POLARIS, not because either is scientifically preferred; (3) POLARIS tiles are an unversioned, mutable plain-HTTP product, so this checksum pins one retrieval and a regeneration may differ slightly; (4) the subset is deliberately tiny (nine cells) to keep one regeneration affordable -- the ingest reads a 2 x 2 degree bounding box, and cost grows with that box, not with the target cell count; (5) coordinates are the pinned sample's float32 cell centres, so consumers matching them to a climate grid should rely on the CLI's spacing-based tolerance rather than exact float equality. Usage: pass as --netcdf_awc with --var_name_awc awc alongside precipitation and PET subset to the same nine cells; the variable is in millimetres and the CLI converts to inches for the Palmer water balance.
